model_annotation: The plot illustrates the share of employed individuals (Anteil Erwerbstätige in %) across different age groups (Alter) for four distinct population groups in Germany. The x-axis represents age, ranging from 20 to 70 years, with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis shows the percentage of employed individuals, ranging from 0% to 100%, also on a linear scale with major gridlines at 20% intervals. Four lines are plotted: a black solid line with circular markers for individuals “ohne Migrationshintergrund” (without migration background), a gray solid line with circular markers for those “in Deutschland geboren” (born in Germany), a light blue dashed line with circular markers for those “zugewandert bis 2009” (migrated before 2009), and a dark blue dashed line with circular markers for those “zugewandert seit 2010” (migrated since 2010). The black line starts at approximately 60% at age 20, rises steadily to around 85% between ages 30 and 55, and then declines to about 5% at age 70. The gray line begins at about 55%, increases to roughly 80% by age 30, fluctuates between 70% and 85% until age 60, and then drops sharply to near 0% by age 70. The light blue line starts at approximately 35%, rises to around 70% by age 30, remains relatively stable between 60% and 70% until age 60, and then decreases to about 10% at age 70. The dark blue line begins at around 38%, fluctuates between 40% and 65% until age 60, and then drops sharply to 0% by age 70. All lines show a steep decline in employment share after age 60, with the black and gray lines remaining higher than the blue lines across most of the age range.
